main_text.l: Vipera ex vtero matris rupto erumpens.
[Woodcut: a viper emerging from its mother's ruptured womb, with arched ruins and a landscape beyond; described under notes.]
VIperei exedunt ceu matris Ʃiscera fœtu-
s: Sic quos ipsa suo fouit alumna sinu,

l.i: At non euentu, nec ratione pari.
Vipera nam salua infelix prole interit, illis
Hac contra extinctis non peritura manet.

page.notes: The woodcut shows a landscape with arched ruins at left, a tree above, a distant town at right, and two vipers in the foreground, one emerging from a body. The initial V of the verse is a large letter. The line "Ʃiscera" reads as printed with a long s-like form; "Roditur" and "nimium" are as printed. Verse lines are set with irregular spacing as printed.
